option.label: Node beard hairs usually erect, mostly 1–3 mm
option.detail: Inspect actual culm nodes. Gould gives hairs mostly1–3mm, occasionally longer, typically erect and not widely spreading. Diggs calls the ring spreading; preserve this source difference.

option.label: Long hairs on UPPER sheath margins / near ligule
option.detail: Leaves are otherwise essentially hairless in Gould. Locate hairs on upper sheath margins and near the ligule, not the blade surface or node beard.

option.label: Straight main axis; many branches, basal ones rebranched
option.detail: Gould gives numerous primary branches4–9cm, erect or loosely spreading at tips; basal ones moderately rebranched. Panicle7–13cm, often partly enclosed by upper sheath.

option.label: Branch joints / pedicels have broad membranous center
option.detail: Inspect the branch internodes and pedicels: thickened hairy margins surround a broad membranous central region. Do not equate this with a narrow terminal groove or a round branch base.

option.label: SESSILE first glume sparsely hairy below middle
option.detail: Inspect the first glume of a sessile spikelet. Gould says usually sparsely hairy below middle; this is not second-glume pubescence or a papilla-based stiff-hair claim.

option.label: SESSILE first glume with glandular pit near middle
option.detail: Gould var.perforata has a pit or depression at or above middle on most/all sessile first glumes. Typical var.barbinodis is mostly/all unpitted. The broad species profile retains both.

option.label: FERTILE lemma awn 20–30 mm or longer
option.detail: Measure the true lemma awn on a sessile fertile spikelet from its attachment, excluding body and hairs. The source gives a lower bound20mm, not a maximum30mm.
